skill.name: auth
skill.description: Guides implementation of server-side authentication and access control for Next.js 15 and Supabase apps, including route protection, RBAC, OAuth, and family-based data isolation.
skill.summary: Build server-side Supabase authentication and access control for Next.js 15 apps.
skill.author: BOM-98

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, file trees, placeholder URLs, and inline code formatting. No prompt injection or executable command behavior was found, but the skill does include high-risk guidance around collecting and storing sensitive PII.

remediation.issue: Registration guidance includes SSN and other sensitive personal data.
remediation.suggestion: Remove SSN from the default flow. Collect sensitive identifiers only when required, and store them in encrypted server-side tables with strict RLS and audit controls.

semantic_findings.description: The skill documents registration data that includes SSN, birthdate, address, and phone details. Copying this pattern without minimization, encryption, and strict access controls creates privacy and compliance risk.

content.value_statement: Authentication mistakes expose user accounts and tenant data. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear patterns for Supabase auth in Next.js.
actual_capabilities: Documents route protection for Server Components, layouts, and Server Actions.
Shows login, logout, registration, email verification, and GitHub OAuth patterns.
Explains role checks for admin and member users.
Lists required auth files, helpers, database tables, and environment variables.
Provides security rules for Supabase token validation and server-only helpers.
limitations: Assumes a Next.js 15 App Router project that already uses Supabase.
Does not provide runnable source files or database migrations by itself.
Examples must be adapted to the target schema and route names.
Does not replace privacy, legal, or compliance review for sensitive user data.

use_cases.title: Protect Dashboard Routes
use_cases.description: Add server-side checks that redirect unauthenticated users before protected dashboard content renders.

use_cases.title: Add Supabase Login Flows
use_cases.description: Implement login, logout, email verification, and GitHub OAuth using existing Supabase helpers.

use_cases.title: Review Tenant Access Rules
use_cases.description: Check that family data access uses server-side authorization and role checks before reading or writing records.

prompt_templates.title: Protect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to protect a new dashboard page in a Next.js 15 app with Supabase auth. Explain the files I should update.

prompt_templates.title: Build Login and Logout
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add login and logout flows using the existing Supabase server client and auth page structure.

prompt_templates.title: Secure a Server Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Server Action and update it to require authentication, handle unauthorized users, and avoid client-side trust.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tenant Authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-tenant admin flow for family accounts with role checks, route protection, and Server Action authorization.

output_examples.input: Protect a dashboard route that only signed-in users can view.
output: Place the authentication check at the top of the dashboard layout.
Redirect unauthenticated users to the login page.
Let child dashboard pages inherit the same protection.
Apply the admin check to the page and related Server Actions.
Hide admin controls from member users.
Return unauthorized users to a safe dashboard route.

output_examples.input: Review family data access for tenant leaks.
output: Verify that each data path uses the current user family identifier.
Require explicit family access checks before updates.
Avoid trusting route parameters without server validation.

best_practices: Validate users on the server before trusting auth state.
Put authorization checks in Server Actions as well as protected layouts.
Keep family and role checks close to data access paths.
anti_patterns: Trusting client-side role checks as the only authorization layer.
Using middleware redirects as the only protection for POST Server Actions.
Copying sensitive PII fields into auth metadata without a privacy design.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js 15 App Router applications that use Supabase authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with Server Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to require authentication and authorization inside Server Actions.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for GitHub OAuth through Supabase.

faq.question: Does it cover role-based access control?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers admin and member checks for pages and Server Actions.

faq.question: Does it create a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples for an existing app structure.

faq.question: Should I store SSN values from the examples?
faq.answer: Do not copy sensitive PII fields by default. Use data minimization, encryption, and compliance review first.
